_comment: What openclaw.json must produce from openclaw.fixture.jsonl. The fixture is a REAL session run on this machine on 2026-09-06 (openclaw 2026.9.2, gemini-3.5-flash), redacted: values replaced, structure untouched. Its last line is deliberately cut — a transcript is appended to while it is read, and the parser must drop that fragment rather than call it format drift.
_traceId: The real export wrote `traceId` and `sessionId` with the SAME value. The fixture deliberately separates them, because a fixture exists to discriminate: with both equal, a connector reading the wrong field passed every assertion. That mutant survived until they were split.
_projectPath: null ON PURPOSE, and this is the finding that cost the most to establish. The trajectory exporter redacts the workspace root to the literal string `$WORKSPACE_DIR`. Mapping it would paint a placeholder into a column meant to name a directory; absent reads as unknown, which is true. There is no branch field at all in the format.
_artifacts: Two files, from the two kinds of evidence, and getting BOTH is the whole point. notes.md was recorded by a `write` tool call (origin 'tool'); second.txt was read out of a redirection inside an `exec` command (origin 'shell'). Reading the exporter's code had predicted these paths would be destroyed by redaction — measurement says otherwise, because OpenClaw's tools address files RELATIVELY and a relative path never carried the workspace root that gets rewritten. Newest first, because the walk runs backwards: the exec came after the write.
